question: Are the proposed head-loss, quote-clock and queue-dynamics interventions coherent, distinct from previous failures, feasible and worth their next experiment?
user_scope: The user requested materially deeper development of all three branches after the preliminary scout.
deliverables: revised ranking and executable next study specifications

baseline.discovery_reference: C equal ft256dH+ft128H+ft128s4H+ftc500H; one-epoch head FT proxies must not silently stand for V1

verification.exposure: All existing data/folds exposed. This round produces mechanism and feasibility evidence, not a new score claim.
verification.metric: Official pooled clipped absolute-target-weighted Pearson, mean over two targets.
verification.unit: Whole chains for data partitions; repeated model seeds are distinct from chain resampling.

allowed: read original server code, logs, checkpoints and data
write bounded new diagnostics/results only in isolated creative worktree or task-specific temporary directory
publish research progress to existing GitHub branch
diagnostic_protocol: Freeze exact sampling, calculation and recipe in a branch-specific plan before running. Use training-side inputs only and report all outcomes, including timeout. Diagnostics may refute feasibility or clarify mechanisms, but do not establish competition improvement. Root schedules any remote diagnostic to prevent resource collisions.
invariants: No edits to original dirty server checkout
No evaluator or previous result mutation
No data leakage via whole-sequence anchoring, current/future labels at serving or class routing
No invented physical interpretation of anonymous codes
stop: One bounded diagnostic recipe per branch, plus deterministic correctness checks; then cross-review and synthesize. No outcome-driven sweeps or new model training in this round.
confirmation: Any future candidate study needs paired controls, serving-ensemble contribution, fixed checkpoint and weights. Existing folds remain exploratory; no fresh confirmation is available in this round.
